newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE makes record advance ahead of budget.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE makes record advance ahead of budget.

text.p: Britain's FTSE 100 share index surged to an all-time record at Tuesday's opening, encouraged by sharp gains in New York overnight and optimism over a "prudent" budget due later in the day.
London's blue-chip index was up 17.5 points at 4,072.1 by 1146 GMT after earlier jumping as high as 4,094.4, a decisive break through its previous high of 4,073.2, set on October 21.
"I don't think anyone had anticipated this 100 point rise in our market over the last couple of days," said one trader.
FTSE 250 stocks were up 6.3 points at 4,428.6 whilst the broader Reuter/HSBC 150 index was up 4.39 points at 11,00.92.
"Wall Street defied the rules of gravity once again so we went off to the races first thing and nearly got to 4,100 but the futures stopped us in our tracks," said another trader.
The Dow Industrials share average soared 76 points or 1.71 percent overnight to breeze through the 6,500 barrier and chalk up its 11th record performance in 12 sessions.

U.S.-quoted FTSE heavyweights like Glaxo-Wellcome and SmithKline Beecham led the gainers in London but stocks turned mixed late morning with gainers outweighing losers by two-to-one as investors targeted selected stocks.
"We are bound to start getting a bit nervous after the initial reaction to Wall Street," said one trader. "People will start trying to pick the winners for the budget," he added.

Traders said they expected to see the corporate sector's tax burden increase in the budget, to offset falls in personal taxes designed to woo the electorate ahead of a general election which must be held by May next year.

The Chancellor is expected to take a penny off the basic rate of income tax. "There will be a rebalancing of the tax burden, hitting the corporate sector," a dealer said. "Everyone but the private sector will probably benefit to some degree."
"But if the budget is sensible it will take some of the pressure off interest rates, and that's what we want to see."
Activity remained thin on caution ahead of the budget statement at 1530 GMT with a modest 415 million shares changing hands by 1118 GMT. But dealers said sentiment remained solid.
"There are not many sellers around and there's no reason to sell," one said. "The market has a good feel to it and we could see momentum picking up again later in the day."
Technical analysts said the bullish sentiment was ignited on Friday after a dramatic advance which saw the FTSE post its biggest one-day gain in 16-months.

"We have a lot of catching up to do with other world markets," said Chris Chaitow, technical analyst at Robert Flemings Securities. "Friday was the key when we crossed 4,000. That was the signal to make new highs and I am still targeting 4,200 for the year-end," he said.
Among early stock features in London, BAT Industries eased to be up 1-1/2p at 460-1/2p after initial gains on the back of the rise in Philip Morris shares overnight.
Glaxo-Wellcome put on 18-1/2p to 10.21-1/2 pounds and SmithKline Beecham was up 12p to 786, both on the strong rise in the U.S. overnight.

Elsewhere, National Grid was unchanged after half year profits dropped to 292.7 million pounds but the company said it aimed to cut core costs by six percent a year. Severn Trent put on 3p to 670-1/2p after its interim results were accompanied by plans for a share buy-back.

Shares in RTZ meanwhile fell 17-1/2p to 964p on profit-taking triggered by a fall in CRA shares and Courtaulds extended its loss amid reaction to results last week. Courtaulds lost 14p to 402-1/2p, a six-month low.
MAM shares reached a record high of 12.37-1/2 pounds, up 34p on the rise in the British stock market.
